descriptors.definition: Control activities are policies and procedures that help ensure management directives to address risks are carried out. They include performance reviews, information processing controls, physical controls, and segregation of duties.
inclusion: Reviewing actual performance versus budgets
Checking arithmetical accuracy of records
Physical security of assets and records
Assigning different people incompatible responsibilities
exclusion: Monitoring activities performed separately by internal audit
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the control environment, which sets the overall organizational tone rather than specific transaction-level rules.

descriptors.concept_name: Information System, Including the Related Business Processes, Relevant to Financial Reporting, and Communication
descriptors.definition: The information system relevant to financial reporting encompasses methods and records that identify, record, describe, measure, determine the timing of, and properly present valid transactions. Communication involves providing a clear understanding of individual roles and responsibilities pertaining to internal control over financial reporting.
inclusion: Procedures to identify and record all valid transactions
Methods to measure transaction values properly
Policy manuals and accounting manuals for communication
exclusion: General operational management decisions unrelated to financial reporting
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from monitoring of controls, which evaluates if established system controls continue to operate effectively over time.

descriptors.definition: Monitoring of controls is a management responsibility involving ongoing evaluations and separate assessments to verify that internal controls operate as intended and are modified for changing conditions. It helps ensure that controls continue functioning effectively over time through internal oversight, internal audit evaluations, and external communications.
inclusion: Management reviews of timely bank reconciliations
Internal auditors evaluating compliance with sales policies
Considering communications from external parties and regulators
exclusion: Initial design and daily execution of transactional control activities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from control activities, which are policies and procedures executed to mitigate specific risks, whereas monitoring evaluates those activities' ongoing effectiveness.

descriptors.concept_name: Review of the System of Internal Controls
descriptors.definition: Evaluating internal controls involves assessing their design capability to prevent or detect material misstatements and verifying their implementation. The review enables auditors to determine the extent of reliance they can place on the internal control system for producing reliable financial reports.
inclusion: Evaluating control design before testing implementation
Assessing manual elements for unusual or non-recurring transactions
Reviewing the mix of manual and automated controls
exclusion: Designing management's internal control business processes
Sole reliance on ineffective controls without design testing
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from mere observation, as it requires structured evaluation of both control design and active implementation.

descriptors.concept_name: Techniques of Evaluation of Internal Control
descriptors.definition: Techniques of evaluation include structured questionnaires that use organized sets of questions across functional areas to assess control effectiveness and detect weaknesses. These questionnaires are typically completed by executives or collaboratively with the auditor to document control systems.
inclusion: Organized sets of questions covering purchases, sales, and receivables
Structured Yes, No, or Not applicable replies
Auditor-assisted or executive-completed review sessions
exclusion: Substantive analytical procedures on account balances
Direct physical inventory counting without control evaluation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from direct substantive testing, as questionnaires focus specifically on evaluating the existence and effectiveness of control systems.

descriptors.concept_name: Reporting to Clients on Internal Control Weaknesses
descriptors.definition: Auditors must communicate identified material weaknesses in internal control to management and those charged with governance on a timely basis, preferably in writing through a management letter. Such communication assists clients in correcting deficiencies but does not relieve the auditor of the duty to report shortcomings by way of audit qualifications where necessary.
inclusion: Written communication of material weaknesses to management or the audit committee
Reporting on absence of adequate controls increasing error or fraud risks
Suggestions for operational improvements
exclusion: Issuing unmodified audit opinions when material misstatements remain uncorrected
Imposing additional responsibilities regarding preliminary risk assessment
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the final auditor's report on the financial statements, as a letter of weakness specifically targets internal control deficiencies.

descriptors.definition: Internal control frameworks guide organizations in building and embedding comprehensive controls into their strategic, governance, and management processes to safeguard business value and achieve objectives. They encompass all activities across operations and reporting rather than being limited strictly to financial functions.
inclusion: Embedding early warning mechanisms into management information systems
Benchmarking financial statements against the financial reporting framework
Controls covering the entire range of operations and activities
exclusion: Standalone risk reporting systems isolated from business processes
Sole focus on narrow financial accounting entries
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from individual control activities, as frameworks provide the overarching structural benchmark for all internal controls within an entity.

descriptors.definition: International internal control frameworks provide structured models consisting of foundational components and detailed principles that organizations use to assess the effectiveness of their internal control systems in achieving operations, reporting, and compliance objectives. The COSO framework specifically categorizes internal control into five components supported by seventeen mandatory principles.
inclusion: Operations, financial reporting, and compliance objectives
Seventeen basic internal control principles
Evaluation of control system effectiveness
exclusion: Unstructured management practices lacking defined governance components
Isolated operational guidelines without enterprise-wide integration
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from national statutory guidance notes by offering a globally recognized comprehensive taxonomy of control components and principles.
